To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the thickness of the flux tube between two static charges is given by a 2D integrability equation, 2) the ratio of k- and fundamental string tensions is given by an integrable 2D equation, 3) the ratio of the Polyakov loops of two charges is given by an elliptic integral.

the following quantities can be expressed in terms of the solution of a 2d integrable system: (a) the ratio of the k-string tensions, (b) the ratio of Polyakov loop correlators in the deconfined phase, and (c) the flux tube thickness in the confined phase.

the deconfining phase transition in the 3D Ising gauge theory is described by the 2D Toda integrable system, and that in the 3d Z(2) gauge-Higgs theory the deconfinment transition is described by the elliptic Calogero-Moser integrable system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the phase structure of gauge theories in three dimensions.
a new class of integrable systems which are related to 3D Lattic Gauge Theories.
the study of the properties of the deconfining phase transition in 3D lattice gauge theories (LGT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the integrable structures in LGT near the deconfined phase transition is an interesting subject to be further investigated.
integrable systems appear in a variety of contexts, but their precise nature depends on the specific observables under study.
integrable systems emerge as a natural consequence of the confinement/deconfinement transition, as a result of the interplay of the large distance and strong coupling limits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
integrability emerges at the deconfining transition as the effective theory for the low energy dynamics of the system.
integrability is an emergent property of 3D Lattices.
, at the deconfining phase transition, the dynamics of the system can be described in terms of 2D classical integrable systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integrable structures are not only present in the continuum limit but are also present in the lattice formulation.
the integrability is a robust property of the theory, that can be used to predict the behavior of the theory at the critical temperature.
